p: First things first: anyone aged 13 or over fishing for freshwater fish in England needs a rod fishing licence from the Environment Agency, on top of whatever ticket the fishery asks for. Licences for 13 to 16-year-olds are free, but they still need one, so sort them out online before the trip and you won't have any awkward moments on the bank.

Most commercial fisheries also have their own house rules on things like hook types, bait, keepnets and unhooking mats. They're there to look after the fish, so read them, follow them and ask if you're unsure. A decent unhooking mat and a landing net are worth packing even if you're only planning a gentle pleasure session.

If you're staying over, the joy of a place like this is the early start without the early drive. Dawn and dusk are often the liveliest times on the water, and having your pitch or holiday home right there means you can make the most of both, then have a lie-down in the middle of the day.

When the rods are packed away, Retford's market square is a pleasant spot for supplies, and the Bassetlaw Museum in the town tells the story of the area. For a bigger day out, Clumber Park, the National Trust estate near Worksop, is within easy reach, with its huge lake, woodland and miles of cycling and walking paths.
